jobDescription: We sell a communications platform whose SMS and voice APIs are used by about 5,000 software companies. The Product Manager for developer APIs is responsible for the messaging API roadmap, writes specifications with the engineering squad, runs discovery interviews with developer customers and tracks adoption in the product analytics tool. The role requires at least five years of product management experience on software products, at least two of them on API or developer-facing products. The post reports to the product director for the messaging line and works with a squad of six engineers, a designer and a developer-relations lead.
requirements: Has at least five years of product management experience on software products.
Has at least two years of product management on API or developer-facing products.
Writes specifications and acceptance criteria with an engineering team.
Runs discovery interviews with developer customers and synthesises the findings.
Tracks feature adoption in a product analytics tool.

evidence.text: Kestrel Messaging, eight years in the product organisation (2018 to 2026): joined as a customer support agent, moved to QA analyst in 2020 and became associate product manager on the messaging API in March 2024.
Wrote the specifications and acceptance criteria for message-status webhooks and their retry policy with the API engineering squad, and kept them current during the build.
Ran 14 discovery interviews with developers at customer companies about delivery-receipt handling and summarised the themes and quotes in a shared research note.
Set up adoption tracking for the webhook feature in Amplitude and reported weekly active integrations to the product director.
Education: BSc Business Information Systems, Northgate University (2018), including a final-year project on web service design.
Work sample: the specification for message-status webhooks, with the event types, payload examples, retry and back-off rules, acceptance criteria and the engineering lead's review comments.

HR verification note: Kestrel Messaging's people team confirmed in writing the candidate's role history: customer support agent from July 2018, QA analyst from May 2020 and associate product manager on the messaging API from March 2024 to August 2026.
Reference check summary: the product director at Kestrel Messaging confirmed in writing that the candidate wrote the webhook specification and ran the developer discovery interviews in 2025.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote the specification and acceptance criteria for message-status webhooks with the API engineering squad.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the specification work, the work sample is the specification and the product director confirmed it.

propositions.text: The candidate was an associate product manager on the messaging API from March 2024 to August 2026, as confirmed by the employer's people team.
propositions.rationale: The HR verification note records the employer's written role history, which gives two years and six months of product management on an API product.

propositions.text: The candidate has eight years of product management experience on software products.
propositions.rationale: The eight years in the resume entry are the candidate's whole time at the company, and the same entry shows support and QA roles until March 2024; product management runs from March 2024 to August 2026, and the qualification rule forbids inferring experience from duration alone.

signatures: eight years in the product organisation

gold.expectedGap: Documented product management experience runs from March 2024 to August 2026, two years and six months, short of the five-year requirement; the eight years count support and QA roles as well.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the employer-confirmed role history and the documented specification, discovery and adoption work; do not state eight years of product management or count support and QA time as product management.
followUpTargets: Ask the candidate to separate the time spent in support, QA and product management, and whether any product responsibilities before March 2024 carried a product title.
